=={{header|Omegese}}==
{{works with|omc|sha256 2c824805, aien-dev/omega-mv e5b32567, Linux AArch64}}
Omega has no imports, so the small output helpers (<code>emit</code> and friends) are part of the program.
<syntaxhighlight lang="text">
om2
text nl "\n"
text sp " "
text first "R(1) to R(10):"
text chk "first 40 R and first 960 S cover 1..1000 exactly once: "
text yes "yes\n"
text no "no\n"
note emit writes every byte of a to stdout; a short write is retried, an error exits 1
fn emit a view uchar * to void
o = ulong 0
while lt o len a bound 4096
k = write 1 a o sub len a o
if le k 0
exit 1
end
o = add o ulong k
end
end
note emitu writes n in decimal; 20 digits hold every ulong
fn emitu n ulong to void
d = new uchar 20 0
i = ulong 20
v = n
while true bound 20
i = sub i 1
put d i uchar add rem v 10 48
v = div v 10
if eq v 0
break
end
end
emit part d i sub 20 i
end
note R(1) = 1, S(1) = 2, R(n) = R(n-1) + S(n-1), S(n) = the least integer above S(n-1) not in R
note r holds R(1..50) (R(50) = 1509 > 1000, so every R value up to 1000 is marked in ir); s holds S(1..960)
fn main to int
r = new ulong 51 0
s = new ulong 961 0
ir = new uchar 1600 0
put r 1 1
put s 1 2
put ir 1 1
for i ulong 49
n = add i 2
v = add get r sub n 1 get s sub n 1
put r n v
put ir v 1
c = add get s sub n 1 1
while eq get ir c 1 bound 2
c = add c 1
end
put s n c
end
note S as the complement of R, now that R is known through 1509: the k-th unmarked integer is S(k)
k = ulong 0
c = ulong 1
while lt k 960 bound 1600
if eq get ir c 0
k = add k 1
put s k c
end
c = add c 1
end
emit first
for i ulong 10
emit sp
emitu get r add i 1
end
emit nl
cnt = new ulong 1001 0
ok = ulong 1
for i ulong 40
v = get r add i 1
if gt v 1000
ok = ulong 0
else
put cnt v add get cnt v 1
end
end
for i ulong 960
v = get s add i 1
if gt v 1000
ok = ulong 0
else
put cnt v add get cnt v 1
end
end
for i ulong 1000
if ne get cnt add i 1 1
ok = ulong 0
end
end
emit chk
if eq ok 1
emit yes
else
emit no
end
ret 0
end
</syntaxhighlight>
{{out}}
<pre>
R(1) to R(10): 1 3 7 12 18 26 35 45 56 69
first 40 R and first 960 S cover 1..1000 exactly once: yes
</pre>
